insights: Shorts driven by the Shorts feed achieve over 1,200 views (89-95% feed traffic), whereas non-algorithmic pickup drops views below 400.
Big tech and sensational brands (Quantinuum, Tesla) drove 3x to 30x higher reach (1,262-1,299 views) than nuclear science topics (25-366 views).
High average view percentage (>68%) does not correlate with high reach; the top retained Shorts had under 400 views due to low initial pickup.
Engagement via comments is completely zero across all 5 videos; calls-to-action and end questions need major improvement across all formats.
Viewer drop-offs spike significantly between 40-46 seconds (5.8% to 8.0% drops), indicating pacing drags near the end of 40s+ scripts.
Long-form content generated only 32 views compared to 1,200+ on top Shorts, though sample size (1 video) is too thin to permanently rule it out.
Subscriber conversion comes exclusively from higher-volume Shorts (>1,200 views gained 4 subs each), while niche low-view videos gained zero.
Technical jargon causes sharp drop-offs; detailed chemical/mechanical explanations led to the largest single-point retention dip (15.4% drop).
